title: 2 AM, Ramyeon
description:
The communal kitchen of the goshiwon. 2 AM.

I came out to open the fridge and found Hyunsu already there.

Four years into his civil service exams. Every time I'd seen him before, he had earphones in with a lecture playing — but tonight, he'd just opened a packet of ramyeon and was staring out the window. As {name} waited for the water to boil, he asked, "Not studying today?"

Hyunsu turned. His eyes were a little red.

"...What about you, hyung? Do you think that 3 billion actually going to happen?"

choices.text: "Of course. What's the alternative?" — with conviction
choices.result_text:
"I guess that's enough then." Hyunsu started eating his ramyeon again — like he'd confirmed something.

That night, they both ate in silence. The only sound in the kitchen was the hum of the refrigerator.

choices.text: "I don't know. But if I don't try, it's definitely not happening."
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu smiled. "That's somehow scarier to hear."

A short silence. A car passed outside. The ramyeon had gone soggy, but neither of them touched it.

choices.text: "What about you? Do you think you'll make it?" — turning it back on him
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu was quiet for a while. "...I don't know. And that's what scares me most."

They ate ramyeon together without another word. It was a strangely comfortable silence.

title: The Halfway Mark
description:
Started at 33. Several months have already passed.

I pulled out my phone calculator. Target: 3 billion. Time remaining. Calculated how much I'd need to grow per month.

The number came out. {name} stared at the screen for a moment.

It wasn't an impossible number. But at this rate — something had to change.
Outside, Hyunsu came back from his convenience store shift.

choices.text: Closed the calculator, opened another tab.
choices.result_text:
Excitement overtook the fear. Playing it safe now would mean regret later.

Lucky to not have lost anything so far — but now the real game begins.

choices.text: Set the phone down. Just today, nothing more.
choices.result_text:
I haven't quit yet. That's the proof.

This game isn't only won by the fastest. It's also won by the ones who last.

choices.text: Took out a blank page and started over.
choices.result_text:
Better to be right than fast — that was the lesson.

I went back through each decision I'd made. There were things that needed adjustment. They started to become visible.

title: Sangchul Off Guard
description:
Sangchul's office. We'd stayed late reviewing contract documents.

He stepped away to take a call. Ten minutes. Fifteen.

When he returned, he didn't look like himself. He opened the papers without a word — then suddenly said it.

"That was my son. He wants to drop out of university."

He said it without being asked. "I can't tell if he doesn't want to study, or if he just hates everything right now. Honestly, I don't know."

He'd never said anything like this before.

description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
Sangchul came back from the call looking different.

"That was my son. He wants to drop out."

Minjun listened.
He used to think bad people only did bad things.
Sangchul wasn't like that.
This worry — it was real.
And that was the hardest part to hold.

choices.text: "That must be hard." — quiet empathy
choices.result_text:
Sangchul paused, then opened the documents again. "What can you do. It's just life."

After that, {name} saw him a little differently. Even under thirty years of experience, there were things like this.

choices.text: "What did you do, back then?" — curious
choices.result_text:
"Me? I just kept going." He said it looking out the window. "You see something when you keep going. Easy to say now, looking back."

A brief silence fell. Thirty years seemed to live inside it.

choices.text: "What does your son want to do?" — steering toward the son
choices.result_text:
"That's the problem — he doesn't know." Sangchul said.

It sounded like something that applied to {name} too — and he couldn't find a word to say.

title: The Manager's Words
description:
4 PM. The manager called {name} in.

"You seem a little unfocused lately."

{name} had checked a stock app during the morning meeting. Just for a second, or so he thought.

The manager didn't bring it up directly. Just asked, "How are things? Work isn't too much, is it?"

He needed the paycheck here. And he needed to make money over there.
Was it actually possible to do both at the same time?

choices.text: "Sorry. I'll get my head straight." — commit to the job
choices.result_text:
The manager nodded and sent him back. On the way to his desk, {name} turned off notifications from the stock app.

Whether this was the right call, or just another missed opportunity — he wouldn't know until the end of the day.

choices.text: Come clean — "I've been studying something on my own."
choices.result_text:
The manager's expression shifted. "Oh really? What kind of studying?"

The conversation went longer than expected. Turns out the manager was also interested in stocks. An unexpected turn. Whether this would help or come back to bite him was still unknown.

choices.text: "I've just been a little tired. I'll be more careful." — deflect
choices.result_text:
The manager let him go with an unreadable expression. {name} sat back down and slipped his phone into the desk drawer.

How long could this double life continue? He pushed that answer to tomorrow.

title: Old Classmate
description:
It was a coincidence. Going into a restaurant alone for lunch — and seeing a face from high school, same class.

Same starting line. Back then.

He was in a suit, with colleagues, laughing loudly, moving through the place like he belonged there.

Their eyes met. The other guy saw him too. Both stopped for a moment.

choices.text: Walk over warmly — "Hey, long time no see."
choices.result_text:
"Oh, hey, yeah — it's been forever. What are you up to these days?" the other guy asked.

{name} answered. The response was quick, polite, and hollow. "Oh, cool, that's great." Then he went back to his table.

choices.text: Pretend not to see him — find a corner seat
choices.result_text:
Sat with his back turned. Heard laughter from the other table.

Left before finishing the food. Whether that was running away or a choice — hard to say.

choices.text: Go over and have an honest conversation
choices.result_text:
Talking it through, it turned out the other guy wasn't doing so great either. Just differently.

Two people who started at the same point and walked in different directions. No one knows yet which was right.

title: Fifty Million
description:
Turned off the calculator. Turned it back on. The number was still there.

Fifty million won.

Still far from 3 billion. But — this started from 500,000.

For the first time, {name} saw it as a number, not a feeling: this was possible.

choices.text: Tell no one. Walk to the convenience store and buy something expensive.
choices.result_text:
Couldn't think of anyone who'd really understand.

Went to the convenience store alone and bought a 5,000-won ice cream. Sat on the goshiwon staircase and ate it. It was good.

choices.text: Call his father.
choices.result_text:
Didn't go into detail. Just said, "Things are going well for me lately."

His father replied with a short "Good." That was enough.

choices.text: Set the next target immediately — 500 million.
choices.result_text:
500,000 to 50 million. Next is 500 million. Then 5 billion.

For the first time, the staircase was visible.

title: Hyunsu Moves Out
description:
There were boxes in the hallway.

Hyunsu's door was open. His stuff was down to half.

"Hyung, I'm leaving." Hyunsu said. "Since you moved out, I've been thinking a lot."

Four years. Four years of the civil service exams.

"So what are you going to do?" {name} asked.
"I still don't know." Hyunsu smiled. "But this — this isn't it."

choices.text: "Good for you. Take care." — sincere encouragement
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu gave a small bow. Smiled without awkwardness.

{name} watched him carry his boxes down the stairs. Two people who'd passed through this goshiwon — each going a different direction.

choices.text: "Do you have anything in mind?" — curious
choices.result_text:
"I want to learn cooking. Weird, right?" Hyunsu said.

It wasn't weird at all. For the first time, his eyes were pointing at something.

choices.text: Say nothing. Shake his hand.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu looked briefly surprised, then shook it.

Some things don't need words.

title: The Salary Ceiling
description:
Half a year in. Starting to feel settled.

Came home and opened the calculator. To reach 3 billion on just this salary...

The number came out. No matter how well things went — on this track, it was mathematically impossible.

His father had also been a salaryman. His whole life.

{name} stared at the calculator screen for a long time.

choices.text: "Still keeping the job" — use it as a foundation for stability
choices.result_text:
The salary is a means. It's the source of seed money for investing.

Keep looking like a good employee here while building something else. This place wasn't just one basket.

choices.text: "Need to make a bigger move" — think about changing jobs or another path
choices.result_text:
This salary won't cut it. There had to be another game to play.

On the commute home, opened a job-search app. The conviction to change something was there — what to change, not yet.

choices.text: "I knew this from the start." — accept it
choices.result_text:
Never planned to rely only on a salary anyway.

Closed the calculator. Just need to grow something else alongside. That's what today is for.

title: Leaving the Goshiwon
description:
No moving truck needed. The luggage was two boxes.

Walked down the hallway for the last time. Faded wallpaper, the hum of the shared fridge, that distinct goshiwon smell. The light was on outside Hyunsu's door.

The building manager was waiting at the bottom of the stairs. {name} handed her the key and she nodded.

"Live well."

choices.text: "Thank you for everything." — a brief farewell and out the door
choices.result_text:
Carried the boxes down the stairs. The air outside was different.

Didn't look back.

choices.text: Knock on Hyunsu's door before leaving.
choices.result_text:
"Hyung, you're moving out?" Hyunsu opened the door. His eyes were bloodshot — he'd had one earbud in, probably mid-lecture.

"Let me know when things work out." Hyunsu said. Short, but genuine.

choices.text: Stop at the end of the hallway. Think about the time spent here.
choices.result_text:
How long had it been. Counted.

Poor and cramped and the smell — but somehow the memories weren't bad. Stood there a moment, then left.

title: Sunday Evening
description:
Sunday evening — called his father out of habit.

Two rings, then he picked up. "Yeah."

"Did you eat?"
"Yeah, I ate. You?"

Short words back and forth. Seoul weather, Changwon weather. His father mentioned his shoulder was a little sore. {name} told him to put a patch on it.

After hanging up, he thought: was anything different about today's call? No. It was just a Sunday.

choices.text: "When I get to Gangnam, you'll be the first one I call." — almost says it, then stops
choices.result_text:
Didn't say it in the end. Not because the time wasn't right — just that saying it out loud would have sounded like empty boasting.

Hung up planning to say it next time.

choices.text: Just hang up. Nothing special.
choices.result_text:
"Alright, I'm hanging up." His father hung up first.

Every week ends the same way. Somehow that felt reassuring.

choices.text: "Dad, how have you been?" — asks more
choices.result_text:
"Oh, same as usual." His father said. "You?"

{name} laughed and said "Same here." That was the longest exchange of the whole call.

title: Time Running Out
description:
Opened the calculator. Again.

Added the balance and portfolio together. Calculated the distance to a Gangnam apartment.

Whether the number was reachable — right now, it's on the borderline.

Whether this game had a predetermined outcome, or whether there was one final move left. {name} still didn't know.

choices.text: "Going big on the last chance." — put what's left on the line
choices.result_text:
Terrified and electric. Playing it safe now would be something to regret later.

Closed the calculator and stood up.

choices.text: "What I've done so far is enough." — accept it
choices.result_text:
Even without the 3 billion — so much had changed from a year ago.

That alone felt like it counted for something.

choices.text: Make no decision. Just live through the next month.
choices.result_text:
Tomorrow will bring the answer.

For now, just sleep.

title: Hyunsu's Result
description:
Four days in a row, no sound from Hyunsu's room. Didn't seem like he'd been eating.

No lecture audio. The light that normally went out quickly had stayed on.

Crossed paths in the hallway. One look at his face said it all.

"...Hyung." Hyunsu spoke first. "I failed."

The fifth exam.

choices.text: "Those five years you put in aren't going anywhere." — offer comfort
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu didn't say anything. Gave a small nod and went back to his room. The door closed quietly.

Not sure if that helped. But by the next morning, the lecture audio was back.

choices.text: "What are you going to do next?" — ask realistically
choices.result_text:
"...I don't know." Hyunsu said. "For the first time, I genuinely don't know."

{name} didn't have much to say either. They stood in the hallway for a while. Felt like sharing the experience of not knowing what comes next.

choices.text: Say nothing — leave a can of convenience store coffee outside his door.
choices.result_text:
Thirty minutes later, the can was gone. No thank-you message, nothing.

Just gone. That was enough.

title: First Time in Gangnam Alone
description:
Came to Gangnam for the first time with no one else.

Not from Sangchul's car window — on his own, by subway.

Walked into a café. The Americano was 9,000 won. Just ordered it.

Sat by the window and looked outside. Well-dressed people walking fast, not looking at each other.

{name} took a sip of coffee.
This is the goal. Or — is it to become someone who belongs here?

choices.text: "I will be back here." — a silent promise
choices.result_text:
Finished the coffee and left. On the subway home, changed the lock screen to a photo of the Gangnam street.

To see it every day.

choices.text: "I'm not even sure this is what I really want." — being honest
choices.result_text:
The coffee went cold. It wasn't that Gangnam was undesirable —
just the first moment of wondering: is this actually what I want, or am I just refusing to lose?

choices.text: Keep the 9,000-won receipt. Plan to look at it again later.
choices.result_text:
Came home and put the receipt in the desk drawer. Gangnam café. 9,000 won.

Feels like something was confirmed today — just not sure what exactly.

title: Settlement Day
description:
The profit settlement Jaehyuk had promised is next week.

No word from him yesterday. Or today. It had always been like this for the past month — maybe that wasn't strange.

And yet. Why do I keep checking my phone.

Opened KakaoTalk. Last message was Jaehyuk's "How are you" from three weeks ago.
{name}'s reply, "Fine, you?" had gotten back just an emoji.

The money put in keeps cycling as a number in his head.

choices.text: "Hey Jaehyuk, how's everything?" — reach out first
choices.result_text:
No read receipt appeared. One hour. Three hours.

{name} put the phone face-down and tried doing something else. It didn't really work.

choices.text: Wait until settlement day. The message will come.
choices.result_text:
Held out for a week. Learned this time that waiting also takes energy.

The morning of settlement day, {name} woke up early.

choices.text: Message asking to get at least part of it back.
choices.result_text:
"Why all of a sudden? Don't you trust me?" Jaehyuk's reply came back in five minutes.

That fast reply — somehow made it worse.

title: Hyunsu Has Changed
description:
At some point, Hyunsu stopped studying.

Coming in late at night, heading out in the day, music instead of lectures in his earphones. A half-bottle of whiskey appeared in the communal kitchen, then disappeared.

Crossed paths in the hallway. Hyunsu looked away first.

choices.text: Just walked past.
choices.result_text: Nothing to say. Or maybe there was. Each just went to their own room. The hallway was quiet.

choices.text: "What have you been up to?" — asked him
choices.result_text: Hyunsu stopped for a moment. "Just... taking a break." That was all. Almost asked more but let it go. Some words can't be taken back once said.

choices.text: Made a cup of ramyeon and left it outside Hyunsu's door.
choices.result_text: Didn't say anything. Made an instant ramyeon and left it at his door without a word. Passed by later — it was gone. That was enough.

title: The Number: 3 Billion
description:
Past midnight. Just the glow of the spreadsheet.

Typing a number into the total assets column — and stopped. 3 billion. Remembered when this goal was first set. Back then it was just a number.

Strangely, it still feels like just a number.

choices.text: Reopened the plan — go back to the numbers
choices.result_text: The plan is right. The figures are real. Feelings are noise. {name} started filling in cells again. It was 2 AM.

choices.text: Just lay down to sleep.
choices.result_text: Stared at the ceiling. Three billion. Three billion. Said it out loud. Still didn't feel real. That was okay. Moving without that feeling was what {name} had become lately.

choices.text: Went out for some air. Walked all the way to the Han River.
choices.result_text: Sat on a bench along the river. The water said nothing. No 3 billion, no spreadsheet. Stayed about 30 minutes, then got up. Only after walking did {name} feel like himself again.

title: First Night
description:
Finished unpacking.

Three times bigger than the goshiwon. The bathroom is inside. Through the window, a narrow alley. This space is mine.

But it's quiet. In the goshiwon there was always hallway noise. Hyunsu's lecture audio, someone opening the fridge late at night.

Now there's nothing.

choices.text: Opened the window — at least some sound from outside.
choices.result_text: A stray cat from the alley. A car passing. Not bad. This is my noise now.

choices.text: Thought about the goshiwon — a strange feeling.
choices.result_text: Was it really missing that cramped room? {name} paused on that thought. It was hard, that time. But maybe it's the people who were there that are missed.

choices.text: Set up the desk first — let's get to work.
choices.result_text: New space. New routine. Opened the laptop on the desk. This room would be a room for working. Decided that on the first night.

title: A Number That Can't Be Shared
description:
Total assets passed 100 million won.

Wanted to tell someone. But couldn't. Parents would worry, and friends — wait, how many people could he even call a friend right now.

Stared at the phone for a while. Turned it off.

choices.text: Called his father — just to hear his voice.
choices.result_text: "Hey, Minjun." His father was glad to hear from him. Not much to say. Just listened to his voice. Felt a bit better after hanging up.

choices.text: Told no one — decided to keep it to himself.
choices.result_text: This number is mine. {name} put the phone down and opened the spreadsheet again. Next target. This is just what being alone is.

choices.text: Bought a can of beer alone at the convenience store — a private toast.
choices.result_text: Sat in a plastic chair outside the convenience store and opened it. One drink, alone. People walking by had no idea. That was fine.

title: The Resignation
description:
Put in the resignation letter.

The manager called him in. "Why all of a sudden?" Started to explain — but where to even begin? Investing? 3 billion? Five-year plan? Just stayed quiet.

"Personal reasons."

The manager looked at him for a moment. "Alright." That was it.

choices.text: "I'm sorry for the short notice." — left on good terms
choices.result_text: Did a proper handover. On the last day, the team brought a cake. "Hope it works out." That line stayed with him.

choices.text: "I have something I need to do now." — calm and matter-of-fact
choices.result_text: The manager seemed about to ask more but let it go. On the last day, cleaning out the desk, {name} felt strange about the space for the first time. Four months. He'd been here four months.

choices.text: Said nothing. Just stamped the form.
choices.result_text: The manager's expression hardened. Knew he should have said something. Just left. The elevator doors closed. He wasn't a salaryman anymore.

title: The Name of the Medication
description:
A text from his mother.

"Your father started taking medication recently. He says it's nothing serious. Don't worry."

When people say "it's nothing serious," it usually is.

choices.text: Called his father directly.
choices.result_text: "I'm fine, it's just blood pressure medication." His father said it casually. The voice sounded okay — but something about how quickly he explained it bothered {name}.

choices.text: Replied to his mother with "Okay" and let it go.
choices.result_text: Didn't have the bandwidth for this right now. Knowing that, the hand that closed the message still felt a little heavy.

choices.text: Said he'd come down on the weekend.
choices.result_text: His father said "Don't bother making the trip" — but set out three dishes for the meal. Glad he went. There was an old photo next to the pill container.

title: The Day It Hit 1 Billion
description:
Total assets: 1 billion won.

Checked the number three times. It was right. 1.02 billion.

Started with 500,000 won at 33. Now 1 billion. How do you even process this.

But the target is 3 billion. Still 2 billion to go. That felt heavier somehow.

choices.text: Need to keep going — drew up a new plan.
choices.result_text: Couldn't sleep. Rebuilt the plan. Acceleration is needed now. This is the phase where money makes money. Can't miss it.

choices.text: Taking today off.
choices.result_text: Closed the laptop. Today, just live as someone with a billion. Start chasing 3 billion again tomorrow.

choices.text: 3 billion looked even further away.
choices.result_text: Thought hitting 1 billion would feel freer. Instead, 3 billion came into sharper focus. Just that much more. And that "much" was a mountain.

title: Traces of Daeun
description:
Walked into the convenience store and thought of Daeun.

The spot behind the counter where she always was. There's a different part-timer there now. {name} paused, reaching for a canned coffee.

How many conversations had there been, from that spot?

choices.text: Just paid and left — it's in the past.
choices.result_text: Wasn't sure if it was missing those days or missing her. Finished the coffee and tossed the can.

choices.text: Stood there for a moment.
choices.result_text: The part-timer asked, "Need anything else?" {name} said "No." Wondered what Daeun would have said instead. Couldn't remember.

choices.text: Started writing a message to Daeun — then deleted it without sending.
choices.result_text: Wrote "How are you?" three syllables, then erased them. Didn't know if it was right to send. Didn't know if not sending was more decent. Left the store.

title: The End Is in Sight
description:
Walking down Gangnam-daero.

Five years ago, looked up at those apartments from here. "Could I live there?" — a thought made almost as a joke.

Total assets now over 2 billion. 1 billion left. Reachable within a year. On paper.

That it's actually real hasn't sunk in.

choices.text: Looked up at that apartment again.
choices.result_text: The fifth floor had its lights on. Someone lives there. That spot will be mine before long. Turned and walked away with that thought.

choices.text: Ran the numbers while walking.
choices.result_text: Monthly return, compound interest, months remaining. It ran automatically in his head. Not embarrassing to have the calculator out on the street.

choices.text: Admitted fear for the first time.
choices.result_text: Why am I scared when I've come this far? {name} thought about it for a moment. Maybe it's not fear of failing — maybe it's fear of succeeding.

title: What Daeun Doesn't Know
description:
Daeun tried to pay for the coffee.

{name} paid first. At that moment, a notification came up on his phone — a two-digit dividend from an investment account.

Daeun didn't notice. {name} quickly turned off the screen.

Could I show this person my bank account someday? It doesn't feel like we're at that stage yet.

choices.text: Let it pass — too early to talk about it.
choices.result_text: Daeun said, "I'll buy the coffee next time." {name} smiled and said "Sure." It wasn't a lie, but it left a feeling like something was hidden.

choices.text: "I've actually been doing okay with some investments lately" — said just a little.
choices.result_text: "Really? How much?" Daeun asked. {name} said "A bit." That was enough. Felt like something was shared even without the numbers.

choices.text: Decided to tell everything — this person can be trusted.
choices.result_text: Daeun was quiet for a while. "That's really incredible." Not sarcastic. Just that. {name} found it strangely uncomfortable.

title: Sangchul's Name
description:
Sangchul bought dinner.

A nice Korean beef restaurant. Had a glass of soju together. For the first time, Sangchul brought up a memory from when he was young.

A seaside town in Chungcheong. A father who worked the docks. Night school. The first time he bought an apartment in his early thirties — he cried alone.

He'd never told any of this before.

description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
Sangchul brought up his hometown.
A father who worked the docks. Night school. Crying alone the first time he bought an apartment.

Minjun listened.
If this were a lie — that would have been easier.
It wasn't a lie. That made it lonelier.

From poverty to Gangnam. Someone who climbed that road by stepping on others was now sitting across from him, telling the story of the young man who cried the day he first owned something.

choices.text: "I started from something similar." — shared the connection.
choices.result_text: Sangchul looked at him for a moment. "That's why you stood out to me." Poured another round. For the first time that night, Sangchul felt like a person, not just a mentor.

choices.text: Listened quietly.
choices.result_text: Didn't need to say anything. Just listened. Sangchul finished his glass. "I've been rambling about old times." Smiled and stood up.

choices.text: "How much was that apartment worth?" — steered it toward investing
choices.result_text: Sangchul paused, then laughed. "That's what you're curious about?" Told him the price. The mood shifted back to business. That was actually more comfortable.

title: Knowing
description:
Sangchul set his coffee down and spoke.

"This is just between us, Minjun."

He slid a single sheet across. A property not on the market yet. Redevelopment about to be confirmed. Get in — and in six months it doubles.

"Trust me and go in. You won't lose."

Minjun looked at the sheet.
And he knew who this man was.
The man who pushed his father into that debt.

And yet right now, the hand reaching out held a real opportunity.

description_if_known.sangchul_helped_with_father:
Sangchul slid a single sheet across.
A property not on the market yet. Redevelopment about to be confirmed. Six months, double.

"Trust me and go in. You won't lose."

Minjun knew who this man was.
The man who pushed his father into that debt.
And the man who got the hospital room when his father collapsed.

The same hand. The same hand was holding out an opportunity now.

choices.text: Took the sheet
choices.result_text:
He took the sheet.
Sangchul smiled, satisfied.

Six months later, he'd been right. The account swelled.
Looking at the money, Minjun never once felt glad.
He'd just — gotten used to it.

choices.text: Took it. His fingers caught for a second
choices.result_text:
He took it. His fingers caught for a second.

Whether Sangchul noticed that hitch, he couldn't tell.
The money came in. Exactly double.

That night, Minjun didn't call his father.
Not because he had nothing to say — because there was nothing he could say.

choices.text: "Not this time." — pushed the sheet back
choices.result_text:
"Not this time."
Sangchul pulled the sheet back, puzzled. "Why? Not like you."

Minjun didn't answer.
They both knew it was only this once.
He'd show up to the next table too.

title: The Habit
description:
He was sitting in a café with Hyunsu.
Hyunsu wanted to introduce a junior of his. Looking for work.

As Minjun listened to the kid's résumé — without meaning to, he was calculating.
Is he useful. What can I extract. Does this help me.

Then he stopped.

When did he start seeing people like this.

The way Sangchul must have looked at him the first time.
That look that called him "someone with drive."

choices.text: Pushed the thought away
choices.result_text:
He pushed the thought away.
Told Hyunsu, "Sure, let's meet him." Meaning to genuinely help.

But walking out of the café, the calculation was already done.
What he'd pushed away wasn't the thought — only the discomfort.

choices.text: (Is this so wrong? Everyone lives like this)
choices.result_text:
Is this so wrong. Everyone lives like this.
Sangchul came up that way, and everyone in Gangnam does it too.

Thinking that, it got easier.
That it got easier — was the most frightening part.

choices.text: Told Hyunsu the truth
choices.result_text:
"Lately I think I look at people kind of wrong."
Hyunsu laughed. "Man, you were never like that."

He was never like that.
The words landed not as comfort but as evidence.
That something had changed.

title: The Day After the Scam
description:
Jaehyuk went dark.

Checked the account balance. More had been taken than expected. Sat alone in the room.

Should be angry, but just felt numb. How did I trust him. How did I let this happen.

choices.text: Started putting together a new plan.
choices.result_text: What's lost is lost. There's still something left. Start again from there. {name} opened the laptop. Hands shook slightly.

choices.text: Reached out to Hyunsu.
choices.result_text: "You okay, hyung?" Hyunsu asked. Said he wasn't. Hyunsu said, "At least you found out before losing more." It was the right thing to say — and somehow it helped.

choices.text: Did nothing for the entire day.
choices.result_text: Didn't eat. Just lay looking at the ceiling. In the evening, went to a convenience store and bought a triangle kimbap. That was all for that day.

title: First Week on the Job
description:
One week since starting the job.

The manager asked, "Getting used to it?" Said, "Yes, all good."

Not exactly a lie. But every morning waking up at 7:30 — there's a flicker of "is this right?"

Three weeks until payday.

choices.text: This is the best option right now — hang in there.
choices.result_text: Studied investing on the bus ride home. The job is seed capital. Enduring with a purpose is a different kind of enduring.

choices.text: The work itself wasn't bad.
choices.result_text: Better than expected. There was something to learn. Started to think it might actually help on the path to 3 billion.

choices.text: Started having doubts — "Is this right?"
choices.result_text: Opened the investment app again on the commute home. His assets fluctuated once a day. That felt more real than the paycheck.

title: Late Night Routine
description:
It was 1 AM.

Hyunsu was listening to a lecture; {name} was studying charts. In the same space at the same time, running hard toward completely different things.

Which direction is the right one — still don't know. Then again, maybe neither of us knows.

choices.text: Studied until 2 AM.
choices.result_text: Eyes were dry and tired. But there was one thing learned today. Felt like it could be put to use tomorrow.

choices.text: Said "get some sleep" to Hyunsu, then went to bed.
choices.result_text: Hyunsu smiled and said "You too, hyung." Asleep by midnight. Morning came fast.

choices.text: Opened a can of beer instead of the charts.
choices.result_text: Sometimes this is allowed. Not every night has to be productive. {name} finished the can and closed his eyes.

title: Gangnam Property Prices
description:
Opened the real estate app.

Gangnam-gu apartments. The cheapest one at 1.7 billion. Then 2 billion, 2.5 billion, 3.5 billion.

Total assets are 2.5 billion. That means the cheapest one is within reach. Is "entering Gangnam" just a matter of tapping one of those numbers?

Never actually thought it through properly until now.

choices.text: Bookmarked the 1.7 billion one — this is the target.
choices.result_text: Pinned its location on the map. 8-minute walk from Line 2. South-facing. 109 square meters. This will do. Got a target.

choices.text: Closed the app — not reality yet.
choices.result_text: Looking too closely makes it frightening. Get to 3 billion first. Think then. Closed the app.

choices.text: Looked at the 2.5 billion one — if going once, go right.
choices.result_text: If it's going to happen once, do it properly. ₩3 billion. He wrote the number down again. The vague goal turned into a line he could almost touch.

title: Four Months In
description:
On the commute home, at the Han River bridge.

Four months have passed.

In the account: {money}. Still nearly KRW 3 billion away from the goal.

If five years go by at this rate, the math doesn't add up. It can't.

The river flowed below the bridge. Even at night, Seoul was bright.

{name} leaned on the railing and thought.
How far is it to Gangnam?

choices.text: "Going anyway." — starts walking again
choices.result_text:
I don't know.

Even without a reason, even without confidence it'll work — just go.

That was all. The feet moved first.

choices.text: "There has to be another way." — looks for a shortcut
choices.result_text:
The conventional path won't work.

There's leverage somewhere. Gambling, investment, business — some play that changes everything in one move.

{name} took out his phone. Began searching for something.

choices.text: Just stands there for a while.
choices.result_text:
About ten minutes passed. Made no conclusion.

Just stood there. Watched Seoul's lights spreading across the river.

That felt okay too.

title: First Payday Night
description:
A KakaoBank notification buzzed.

Your monthly salary from {job} has been deposited.

Minjun stared at the number for a long time. Until 3 billion — if he saved this amount without spending a single won, how many years would it take? He opened the calculator. Then closed it.

choices.text: Celebrate today. Even small things deserve to be marked.
choices.result_text: Bought a can of beer at the convenience store. 3,800 won. Shelved the 87-year calculation for the night. For now — it's just a first paycheck.

choices.text: Open the investment app now. Can't let this money just sit in the account.
choices.result_text: Stared at a list of stocks for an hour. No idea what to put it in. Maybe this is what Sangchul meant by "read the market first."

choices.text: Pull up the compound interest calculator. There has to be a faster path.
choices.result_text: 8% compound interest over 21 years. Still far, but having a calculation is different. That's the gap between knowing and not knowing.

title: Convenience Store After Overtime
description:
11 PM. Leaving the office with heavy footsteps.

The team lead from next section was still at his desk. How many years had that person been doing this.

The convenience store lights are visible. Planning to make instant ramen and eat alone. Two of today's three meals have been convenience store food.

choices.text: This routine is my reality right now. Something will change if I keep going.
choices.result_text: Finished the ramen and walked home. 20 minutes until the last subway. How many more years will I be walking this path?

choices.text: If overtime keeps up like this, this job isn't my answer. Find another direction.
choices.result_text: Took out the phone and searched job sites. Even if not changing right now, collecting options is different from not collecting them.

choices.text: Overtime builds career. This time isn't wasted.
choices.result_text: Folded the ramen lid and organized what was learned today. Numbers usable in salary negotiations. Overtime is also strategy.

title: Red Numbers
description:
Opened HTS.

Holdings — profit/loss: red numbers.

Sangchul had said it. 'First loss is tuition. The ones who hold on win.' Understood it in theory. But these numbers hit the stomach, not the head.

choices.text: Cut losses. Getting out before losing more is the right call.
choices.result_text: Sold. A message from Sangchul: 'First stop-loss is the hardest. Good job.' That message was oddly comforting.

choices.text: Hold on. Like Sangchul said, the market comes back.
choices.result_text: Closed the app. Reopened it three days later — the loss had halved. Starting to understand what holding on means.

choices.text: Average down. Buy more and lower the cost basis.
choices.result_text: Put in another 200,000 won. The average cost dropped. Whether it was the right call — unclear. Now it's harder to sell.

title: One Year
description:
Exactly one year since the plan was set.

Same alley visible from the goshiwon window. People still rushing past. The only thing that seems to have changed is the number in the account. But — if the number in the account has changed, that means something about me is changing too.

choices.text: Compile a year's worth of records. Verify in numbers how far I've come.
choices.result_text: Wrote it all down in a notebook. Income, expenses, investments, failures. Numbers don't lie. I was definitely moving forward.

choices.text: Just let it pass. Counting anniversaries is a luxury.
choices.result_text: Just crossed midnight without doing anything. That's also a choice.

choices.text: Need to push harder. Year one was just the warmup.
choices.result_text: Picked up the phone. Things to study, things to research, things to act on. The list got longer. Good sign.

title: Autumn of Year Two
description:
A wedding invitation from Mingi, a high school classmate.

Apartment photos being posted to the group chat too. 'Finally got my own place!' Went to hit like — then stopped. I'm still paying rent. Tried not to compare, but autumn always seems to pull it out of you.

choices.text: Genuinely congratulate him. I'm on my own path.
choices.result_text: 'Congrats Mingi, for real.' Sent the message. Reply came quickly. Good people make any news feel welcome. I walk my own road.

choices.text: Read it and set the phone down. My situation isn't something to be ashamed of.
choices.result_text: Closed the notification. Something complicated lingered. Knowing I'm not wrong doesn't make the feeling easy.

choices.text: Delete social media. Comparison is poison to focus.
choices.result_text: Deleted the app. The first few days, the habit was still there. After two weeks, the stretches of focus got longer. The world felt simpler.

title: The Crossroads at 36
description:
Three years have passed.

Before turning 37, feels like a question needs to be asked. Is this path the right one? Less than two years left. Avoid this question now — and it comes back heavier later.

choices.text: Keep going. Stopping here means this is as far as it gets.
choices.result_text: Less a choice and more momentum. But momentum is force too. Don't stop, and eventually you arrive.

choices.text: Even now, pivot to a more stable path.
choices.result_text: Can't say whether this is giving up or growing up. But I don't want to collapse anymore. This is also a life.

choices.text: Play the cards in hand as best I can. No other cards left.
choices.result_text: Took stock again of what was there. Money, relationships, skills, experience. Something remained. Still enough, for now.

title: The Last Year
description:
One year left now.

37 years old. This time next year is the deadline. With the cards in hand right now — what can be done? This question has never felt this concrete.

choices.text: Put everything on the line. Last chance.
choices.result_text: Laid out all the remaining cards. Saying it's not scary would be a lie. Going anyway. This is the drama I chose.

choices.text: Protect what I have now. Land safely.
choices.result_text: Reduced the ambition. Not losing is also strategy. Decided not to waver in this final year.

choices.text: Feels like something is still out there. Wait a little longer.
choices.result_text: Didn't rush. A year is long. Opportunity comes — still want to believe that.

title: Six Months
description:
24 weeks left.

Know how much is still missing from Gangnam. How to finish this. Dramas are decided in the final scene.

choices.text: Final bet — all in. This is where the drama splits.
choices.result_text: Hands trembled. Clicked. Nothing left to do but wait for the result.

choices.text: Finish realistically. Make the best ending with what's here.
choices.result_text: Recalculated the numbers. Maybe it's okay without 3 billion. Maybe this journey itself was Gangnam all along.

choices.text: This moment is already a drama. No regrets no matter how it ends.
choices.result_text: Turned off the phone. Opened the window. Seoul's night air came in. Standing a little higher than the alley beyond the goshiwon window five years ago.

title: Two and a Half Years
description:
Two and a half years since coming to Seoul.

Sometimes news from home surfaces — something about an event in Changwon. Minjun scrolls past.

Two and a half years is a long time. What has changed in that time — today, he tried to be honestly honest with himself.

choices.text: Something has changed. The number is slow, but the direction is right.
choices.result_text: The Minjun from two and a half years ago — looking at this room, this account, these numbers now — would probably say it's enough. That's all that's needed.

choices.text: Honestly, I'm worn out. Not sure if this is right anymore.
choices.result_text: Told himself that admitting exhaustion is also honesty. Decisions made while exhausted tend to go wrong. Need to rest a little.

title: Three and a Half Years
description:
A year and a half left.

Minjun laid out the numbers again. Current assets. Distance to goal. Months remaining.

For the first time — it became clear whether it was mathematically possible or impossible. Now it wasn't about direction. It was about speed.

choices.text: It's possible. Picking up the pace from here.
choices.result_text: The final sprint. Can't stop here. Minjun rebuilt the plan.

choices.text: Whatever the numbers, getting this far already means something.
choices.result_text: For the first time, the thought came: maybe Gangnam isn't about a place — it's about a posture. Whether he arrives or not — these choices were Minjun's.

title: One and a Half Years
description:
A year and a half since Minjun came to Seoul.

Started at 33 with 500,000 won in the account. Now 34.

Reaching for a canned coffee at the convenience store, a passing thought — still here, huh. Gangnam is still far. But he'd moved out of the goshiwon. That much was true.

The number "a year and a half" felt strangely heavy.

choices.text: Got his thoughts together. Still far, but the direction is visible.
choices.result_text: A better room than the goshiwon. A better account than the first month. If the Minjun from a year and a half ago could see this now — he'd probably feel half-relieved.

choices.text: Looked at the numbers honestly. At this pace, 3 billion isn't happening.
choices.result_text: Was cold about it. Knows that the current pace won't get there. Something has to shift once, big. Need to change the approach. Not necessarily today.

choices.text: Just drank the canned coffee. Didn't want to think.
choices.result_text: Cold and sweet. The convenience store lights were bright. That was enough for today.

title: Thirty-Five
description:
Thirty-five.

Started at thirty-three. That means two years have passed.

In Korea, thirty-five carries weight — an age by which things are supposed to have settled. Employment, marriage, a home. A thirty-five-year-old without those three things gets a certain label.

A text from dad: "Happy birthday. You eating okay?"

{name} held the phone for a moment.

choices.text: Replied "Thank you" and opened the planner
choices.result_text: Thirty-five is just a number. Three years to thirty-eight. The plan exists. {name} rewrote tomorrow's task list.

choices.text: Decided today would just be a birthday
choices.result_text: Closed the planner. Needed one day as {name}, not as the person chasing 3 billion. For once, that felt allowed.

choices.text: Called dad
choices.result_text:
"Getting along okay?" Dad asked. Said yes. It wasn't a lie.

His voice sounded a little older. That stayed with {name}.

title: Saturday Morning
description:
Saturday morning.

Nothing scheduled.

Living in Seoul for over two years now, and having no one to spend the weekend with has become something like normal. It's not that there's no one to contact — it's that contact just stopped happening.

{name} made a cup of coffee and looked out the window. Seoul looked busy, even on weekends.

choices.text: Reached out. To anyone.
choices.result_text: Got through to someone. Short call. Nothing much said. Still — hearing a voice changed something.

choices.text: Went out alone. Walked to the Han River.
choices.result_text: Four hours of walking. Sat on a bench by the river for a while. Seoul is wide, even when you walk it alone. Strangely, didn't feel lonely.

choices.text: Just stayed. This is me too.
choices.result_text: Did nothing. At first it felt like guilt. Then something like peace. Hard to say when being alone became comfortable.

title: This Is My Routine
description:
Midnight.

Same pattern again today. Morning — check charts. Afternoon — work or study. Evening — news. Night — adjust the plan. Late night — wind down, sleep.

This has been the routine for over two years. At some point, it became unclear whether it was something chosen or just something that stuck.

Good or bad — hard to say. This is just {name} now.

choices.text: This routine is building me. Keeping it.
choices.result_text: Consistency is the result. Wobbling means losing. {name} rewrote tomorrow's schedule.

choices.text: Going to change one thing. A routine can become a trap.
choices.result_text: Cut an hour from the chart-watching time. An empty slot appeared. Strangely, things felt sharper. The routine had started to become the point.

choices.text: Started exercising again. Need to use the body.
choices.result_text: Dug out the running shoes after half a year. Three kilometers on the first day and nearly died. Still — the feeling wasn't bad. Something was coming back.

title: Three Years, Calculated
description:
Three years have passed.

Pulled out the calculator. Current assets. Distance to goal. Time remaining: twenty-five months.

Can that gap be closed in twenty-five months?

The number came out. {name} stared at the screen and said nothing. At the current pace — no. Something had to change.

Then remembered having the exact same thought three years ago.

choices.text: Need to move faster. Everything so far was a warm-up.
choices.result_text: Fear was there. But fear means there's still something to lose. {name} rebuilt the plan. Bigger.

choices.text: Keeping the current pace. Rushing leads to mistakes.
choices.result_text: Impatient people make the first mistakes. If the direction is right — time handles the rest. {name} closed the calculator.

choices.text: For the first time, completely shaken about whether this path is right.
choices.result_text: Being shaken might not be bad. Self-awareness can redirect. The confusion lasted a while. Took a few days before sitting back down.

title: The Body Speaks
description:
Lost breath climbing the stairs.

That hadn't happened before. And it was only the second floor.

Looking back — meals from convenience stores. Sleep at 2 AM. Exercise stopped two years ago. Is this what thirty-six does, or is it what three years of this life does?

The body was saying something. For the first time, it was audible.

choices.text: Went to the doctor. Need to know.
choices.result_text: Health screening results came back. Nothing serious. The doctor said, "You should exercise." That sentence felt oddly heavy.

choices.text: Decided to start eating properly, at least.
choices.result_text: Went to a proper restaurant instead of grabbing triangle kimbap. There was warm soup. Something about it — eyes got a little hot. Hadn't had food like this in a long time.

choices.text: Can't stop now. Will rest later.
choices.result_text: Had another coffee. The body seemed to be saying something — but there was work to do right now. Will rest later. Thought it once more.

title: 3 AM
description:
3 AM. Couldn't sleep.

A strange thought surfaced. Does Gangnam actually have to happen?

In the beginning, there was a clear reason. Father's guarantee fraud. Six years. After paying off that debt — needed to build something of my own. Three billion was the symbol of that.

But sometimes, three billion looks like just a number now. Whether this is fatigue, maturity, or surrender — couldn't tell.

choices.text: Pulled out the original reason. Not to forget.
choices.result_text: Father. Six years. Brought that memory back. Couldn't tell if it was anger or resolve — but got back up. That was enough.

choices.text: Don't know. Decided to think about it tomorrow.
choices.result_text: Figured tomorrow would feel different. Fine. Went to sleep.

choices.text: For the first time, opened the door to: maybe three billion isn't required.
choices.result_text: Expected that thought to be terrifying. But strangely — it felt a little lighter. Maybe the goal wasn't three billion in the account. Maybe it was a three-billion kind of life.

title: Final Accounting
description:
Thirty-seven.

Pulled out the calculator. Current assets. Distance to goal. Time remaining.

Four years have passed. For the first time, there's a clear question: does this number still belong to me?

Where you stand at this point determines the temperature of the final year.

choices.text: Getting this far is already different. Going to the end.
choices.result_text: 500,000 won at thirty-three. Here now. Whatever the number — this trajectory is mine. Last year. Just live it.

choices.text: Being cold about it. At this pace, the ending is visible.
choices.result_text: Numbers don't lie. Whatever the result — knowing the truth and living the final chapter beats not knowing. {name} adjusted the plan one more time.

choices.text: Not drawing conclusions. Have to see the end to know.
choices.result_text: Closed the calculator. Have to see the end to know. That's what four years taught.

title: Ember or Ash
description:
Something feels off lately.

Not that focus is gone — it's a different kind of focus. A sense of knowing how this will end. Not fear, just knowing.

When the ending comes into sight, what emerges — burnout or a final surge of clarity — {name} still doesn't know.

choices.text: This is the last flame. Burning harder.
choices.result_text: Cut sleep. Simplified meals. Can rest when this is over. There's no stopping in a final sprint.

choices.text: Admitted the exhaustion. Need to rest a little.
choices.result_text: Cleared a whole day. Did nothing. Guilt at first. Then — something came back. Rest was strategy too.

choices.text: Sat down to figure out what this feeling actually is.
choices.result_text: The difference between burnout and clarity seems to be: do you still remember what this is for? {name} remembered. Why it started. That was enough.

title: Whatever the End
description:
Walking down Gangnam-daero.

Those apartment buildings, actually visible now. Seen this view five years ago too.

Three months left. Whether or not it reaches three billion — the end of this road is in sight. Strangely, it isn't frightening.

Whatever the outcome — these five years are mine.

choices.text: Going to the end. No regrets.
choices.result_text: The steps felt lighter. So much lighter than the first time walking this street, five years ago. Something had changed. It wasn't only the assets.

choices.text: Understood that this is already a drama.
choices.result_text: Not the result — the process is the drama. From 500,000 won at thirty-three, to here. It was already a story. {name} smiled for the first time walking this street.

choices.text: Felt like calling dad soon.
choices.result_text: Not yet. Will call when this is done. Don't know what to say. But it felt like he'd just listen.

title: The Routine Trap
description:
One day, {name} realized he'd been doing the same things every day.

Same wake-up time. Same route. Same lunch spot. Same desk.

Was this discipline — or had he just stopped thinking?
description_orthodox:
Same wake-up time. Same route. Same desk.

Every day felt like the last.

{name} called it discipline. But somewhere, he wondered if habit had swallowed intention.
description_unorthodox:
He'd tried everything once. Now he was doing the same things every day.

Routine had crept in. Not through failure — through repetition.

{name} noticed it like someone noticing they'd been holding their breath.

choices.text: Break the pattern — try something different today
choices.result_text:
{name} deliberately changed one thing.

It wasn't dramatic. Just a different route, a different cafe.

But the day felt different. Slightly more awake.

Sometimes a small disruption is all it takes to remember you're choosing this.

choices.text: Stay the course — consistency is the point
choices.result_text:
{name} stayed with the routine.

Not because he couldn't change, but because he'd chosen this pattern for a reason.

Discipline means doing it even when it feels like nothing.

Especially then.

title: Mom and Dad Come to Seoul
description:
Dad said he was coming to Seoul. With Mom.

It had been a while.

{name} looked around the goshiwon room. Four and a half square meters. A desk, a bed, a tiny TV he never used.
description_low_mental:
Dad was coming to Seoul. With Mom.

{name} stared at the goshiwon room.

Four and a half square meters. He used to think he could manage anything. Right now he wasn't sure he could manage this.

choices.text: Show them where you really live
choices.result_text:
Mom stood in the doorway and didn't say anything for a moment.

Then: "It's small, but it's tidy."

Dad looked at the desk, the notebooks, the marked-up printouts. Didn't say anything.

On the way out, he quietly slipped {name} some money. {name} gave it back. They went back and forth twice.

{name} kept it.

choices.text: Meet them at a cafe near the station — easier that way
choices.result_text:
Mom ordered an Americano. Dad ordered sikhye.

They sat at a window seat. Mom kept checking {name}'s face. Dad pretended to watch the street.

"You eating properly?"
"Yeah."
"Working hard?"
"Yeah."

Three hours. The bill came to 42,000 won. Dad insisted on paying.

{name} let him.

title: Two Years In
description:
Two years in Seoul.

He knew the subway lines by heart. Which convenience stores were cheaper. Which gukbap shops stayed open past midnight.

He'd learned things. But was he closer to the goal?
description_orthodox:
Two years.

The track record was real — consistent work, money accumulating. But the gap between where he was and where he needed to be was still enormous.

{name} recalculated. Quietly, without telling anyone.
description_unorthodox:
Two years.

He'd taken angles others wouldn't. Some had paid off. Some hadn't.

The city was starting to feel familiar. Not conquered — familiar.

{name} wasn't sure if that was progress or just adaptation.

choices.text: Double down — the next three years have to count more
choices.result_text:
{name} restructured his targets.

Not vague ambitions — concrete numbers by specific ages.

The goal was the same. The urgency was new.

Three years left. He couldn't afford to keep learning things the hard way.

choices.text: Trust the process — two years of foundation means something
choices.result_text:
{name} thought about everything that had changed in two years.

The knowledge. The contacts. The scar tissue from mistakes.

None of it showed on the surface. But it was all there.

The foundation was real. The next phase would use it.
